text:
maria: Hey folks — running a POC with Acme and hitting 403 invalid_api_key on every /v1/generate call. Customer says they pasted the key from the console. cURL below, response body just says 403 + request_id. anyone free to triage?

maria: curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX_REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"test"}'

alex: can you paste the full JSON error body and request_id? quick guess: org/project mismatch or missing scope. also which org is the customer running under?

maria: Error body: {"error":{"type":"unauthorized","message":"invalid_api_key","request_id":"req_01F4XYZZ"}}. Customer org is org_acme_99, they said they created a key in Console under their org.

devon: grabbing infra logs for req_01F4XYZZ...

devon: log snippet: "timestamp=2026-03-20T14:01:12Z level=warn msg="unauthorized: api_key project mismatch" details="key_org=org_acme_42 request_org=org_acme_99 key_scopes=[console,read] required=[inference.invoke]" request_id=req_01F4XYZZ"

alex: ok that matches. The key they provided belongs to a different org (org_acme_42) and it also lacks the inference scope. Two issues: org mismatch and scope.

maria: they literally copied the key from a different org workspace — oops. what's the fastest remediation for POC?

devon: Fast path: rotate/create a new API key from the correct org/project and ensure you select the inference scope (or full token for POC). Then update the POC env var REDWOOD_API_KEY. If you can't rotate, you can set header "X-Redwood-Org: org_acme_42" to force routing to the key's org but that's only appropriate if the customer actually wants that org. Not recommended for long-term.

alex: test curl to validate (example):

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_NEWKEY_FROM_ORG99" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org_acme_99" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"hello"}'

alex: also check project-level permission: if the POC uses a project-scoped key, make sure the request includes "project_id": "proj-abc" in the body or the key is created within that project.

lisa: I created a new key in org_acme_99 -> project "poc-eval" with scopes [inference.invoke, embeddings.create]. Pasted into the POC env.

lisa: oncall-bot audit: APIKeyCreated id=ak_live_7fz by=lisa@redwood at=2026-03-20T14:07:05Z org=org_acme_99 project=poc-eval scopes=[inference.invoke, embeddings.create]

maria: updating env now...

maria: Updated. retrying...

maria: SUCCESS — generation returned 200 and content. thanks all :tada: :thumbsup:

devon: great. leaving notes for the customer: 1) Always create keys inside the intended org/project. 2) Keys need inference scopes for generation calls. 3) For troubleshooting, include request_id (req_XXXXX) so we can map to infra logs quickly.

alex: I'll add a short checklist to the POC doc and ping SE docs to remind about X-Redwood-Org header and project_id body param.

maria: thanks team — closing the swarm.

oncall-bot: AuditLog: APIKeyUsage id=ak_live_7fz request_id=req_01F4XYZZ status=200 endpoint=/v1/generate by_ip=34.85.12.7

maria: marking as resolved in CRM and adding note about key owner confusion.
